claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation forwards every diagnostic whose location is not in source, including Location.None. The two newly metadata-safe diagnostic constructions produce exactly that location for metadata members, so MsgPack004/005 can now be reported without a location in the consuming project. That contradicts the new documentation and the recorded convention that such member diagnostics belong to the defining assembly; because MsgPack004 and MsgPack005 are errors, it can also break the consuming build.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile a metadata library containing [MessagePackObject] generic struct Item<T> with a public property lacking [Key], then compile an app whose [MessagePackObject] has an Item<int> member and run MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer on the app. Assert that the app receives neither AD0001 nor MsgPack004 for Item<T>.Value. The changed !diagnostic.Location.IsInSource branch currently forwards the Location.None MsgPack004.

claim: The new location filter does not drop metadata-symbol diagnostics that have been converted to Location.None. For a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly with a public member lacking [Key], the null-safe MemberNeedsKey path creates MsgPack004 with a null location; !diagnostic.Location.IsInSource is then true, so the consumer compilation receives a locationless MsgPack004 error. This both contradicts the helper's stated behavior and analyses metadata types that the defining assembly owns.
